title: POC resource scrub and contingency playbook
content:
POC Resource Scrub & Contingency Playbook
Customer: ACME Retail (example)
Prepared by: Maya Chen (solutions-eng)
Date: 2024-11-05 (working doc)

Purpose
- Rapidly validate that we have the right compute, networking, access, and operational playbooks to run a 4-week POC for an inference-heavy catalog personalization feature.
- Provide a clear contingency ladder so the delivery team can keep the POC within SLOs even when capacity or integration issues occur.

Scope
- Focus: hosted/dedicated hybrid - initial proof uses Redwood-hosted models + a Dedicated fallback pool for peak hours.
- Excludes: long-term data residency (will be addressed in Private offering follow-up).

Brief POC summary (for context)
- Goal: demonstrate 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 3:1 user:session mix and reduce API cost per request by ~20% vs baseline.
- Workloads: short prompts (product title + user context) with embedding lookups and generation of 1–3 candidate recommendations.
- Expected QPS: 8 steady-state, 40 spike for 5–10m during catalog sync windows.

High-level timeline (four-week sprint)
- Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): access, quota, initial capacity reservation, test harness.
  - Action: reserve 4 dedicated GPUs (g5x2-equivalent) for dedicated pool on day 0. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2024-11-07.
  - Action: create test dataset (10k queries) + baseline metrics. Owner: Lena. Due: 2024-11-06.
- Week 1 (integration): API integration, key rotation, routing policy smoke tests.
  - Deliverable: end-to-end call including embedding -> rerank -> generate. Owner: Noah. Due: 2024-11-12.
- Week 2 (load & perf): synthetic stress, KV cache tuning, batching policy config.
  - Deliverable: recommended batching/caching config and cost estimate. Owner: Diego. Due: 2024-11-19.
- Week 3 (user validation): run subset of customers, capture quality/regression signals, collect success metrics.
  - Deliverable: final metric snapshot and rollout plan. Owner: Maya. Due: 2024-11-26.
- Week 4 (wrap + handoff): knowledge transfer and next-step proposal.

Roles & escalation
- SE Lead: Maya Chen (primary customer point-of-contact). Escalation: @maya (Slack), maya@redwood.com
- Infra/Capacity: Ravi Patel (reserve/dedicated pools). Escalation: oncall infra (pager: infra-rot).
- Perf Engineer: Diego Alvarez (load tests & KV cache).
- Integration Engineer: Noah Kim (SDK + sample app).
- Customer success: Lena Ortiz (SLA/account coordination).

Resource inventory (initial scrub)
- Compute reserved: 4x g5x2-equivalent reserved on Dedicated pool (buffer: +25% burst).
- Hosted capacity: default service quota 50 vCPU / 200GB memory (verify on 11/06).
- Network: VPC peering planned for secure catalog pulls, CIDR documented in Confluence link.
- Secrets: KMS access required for customer API key; grant scoped service account.
- Access: Customer dev key, read-only S3 credentials for catalog, test user list (10K).

Capacity assumptions and thresholds
- Baseline per-request p95 tokens = 120 tokens generated + 16 embedding tokens.
- Estimated tokens/sec per GPU: 5000 tokens/sec (conservative).
- Autoscale triggers: scale up when 75% GPU utilization for 2m; scale down after 5m below 40%.
- Contention threshold: if queue length > 50 requests and p95 latency > 400ms -> trigger fallback plan.

Model matrix & fallback strategy
- Primary: small-medium open model (quantized Llama-3-8B-q4) — target cost/perf sweet spot.
- Fallback A: Llama-2-7B (lower latency, lower quality).
- Fallback B: Cached candidate set + rule-based reranker (no generation) for catastrophic capacity shortfall.
- Routing policy: prefer Dedicated for steady traffic, use Hosted for burst; if Hosted overloaded, route to Dedicated; if Dedicated overloaded, route selected traffic to Fallback B (degraded mode).

Risk register (top items)
- RISK 1: Dedicated pool not provisioned in time -> Mitigation: short-term burst to Hosted with throttling; pre-notify account ops. Owner: Ravi.
- RISK 2: Embedding ops are unexpectedly costly -> Mitigation: move embedding compute to periodic offline pipeline + cache vectors; reduce embedding frequency. Owner: Diego.
- RISK 3: Data access delays (S3 permission) -> Mitigation: scoped pre-signed URLs + test artifact in demo bucket. Owner: Lena.
- RISK 4: Quality regression when using smaller model -> Mitigation: pre-built eval set + acceptance threshold; gate deployment with A/B test 5% traffic. Owner: Maya.

Contingency ladder (step-by-step)
1) OBSERVE: Alert fires (p95 > 400ms or error rate > 1%) -> Oncall notified via PagerDuty.
2) MITIGATE IMMEDIATE: Enable reduced response mode (Fallback B) via console toggle. Communication: post to #acme-poc-status with short blurb and ETA.
3) SCALE: If mitigation insufficient, request burst capacity from infra (Ravi) and increase dedicated pool by +2 GPUs.
4) ROLLBACK: If recent model change correlates to errors, roll model to previous stable version (document PR and time).
5) POSTMORTEM: Ensure RCA and corrective actions are logged, attach to JIRA-ACME-1423.

Playbook snippets (commands & runbook pointers)
- Reserve GPUs: infra CLI -> redwood infra allocate-dedicated --pool acme-poc --gpus 4 --expires 2024-11-30
- Toggle degraded mode: POST /admin/v1/feature-flags/body {"flag":"acme_poc_degraded_mode","value":true} (ops token required)
- Roll model: POST /v1/models/route -> {"route":"acme-recommend","model":"llama-3-8b-q4@2024-10-02"}
- Load test script: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts/load_test_acme.sh

Workshop agenda (day 0 onsite/remote)
- 09:00 — introductions & goals (15m)
- 09:20 — customer architecture walkthrough (20m)
- 09:45 — Redwood runtime & routing explanation (25m)
- 10:15 — integration checklist and access handoff (30m)
- 10:50 — quick smoke test (30m)
- 11:30 — resourcing & contingency Q/A (20m)
- 12:00 — next steps and immediate actions (10m)

Pre-work checklist (customer action items)
- Provide S3 read-only credentials for demo dataset.
- Confirm service account and KMS access for secrets.
- Approve traffic routing policy for 5% canary.

Acceptance criteria (minimum)
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms during steady-state testing; p99 <= 800ms.
- Errors: overall error rate < 1% during test window.
- Quality: enrichment CTR delta <= -2% vs baseline for candidate generation on holdout set.
- Cost: demonstrable per-request cost <= 0.8x of baseline in recommended config.

Open questions / unknowns
- Does ACME require a pinned model version for audit? (ask legal/compliance).
- Are there catalogue synchronization windows that could cause predictable spikes beyond 40 QPS? If yes, we need scheduled pre-warm.
- Will customer accept degraded mode where generation is replaced by reranking?

Templates
- Slack status post (short): "ACME-POC: p95 elevated, degraded mode enabled, ETA 20m. Owner: Maya. Details: <link>"
- Email to account owner: short summary and ask for permission to increase Dedicated pool by +2 GPUs for 30m.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep test harness small and reproducible (docker image build id in PR).
- Capture all experiments as small notebook with seeds so can reproduce evaluation score drift.
- If we repeatedly hit fallback, schedule a model/quantization tuneback workshop with Research.

Appendix: quick checklist (tick boxes for each action)
- [ ] Reserve Dedicated GPUs
- [ ] Create test dataset and baseline metrics
- [ ] Provision customer S3/KMS keys
- [ ] Smoke test end-to-end call
- [ ] Run 10m 2x spike load test
- [ ] Collect quality metrics + snapshot
- [ ] Deliver final recommendations & cost estimate

End of doc — working draft. Update as actions complete and link final runbook to Confluence page.
